COORDINATOR RULING (owner=user writes; applies to every difficulty, given to reworkers and auditors alike):
The instantiate skill requires every tree to hold one customer's-own write and names "a payment, an instruction, a confirmation" as such writes. The blueprint difficulty summaries' sentences "the agent places orders / bills seats, upgrades and renewals" are base background (logged BLUEPRINT-KNOWN); they do not by themselves make a customer-completed payment illegal. An owner=user write is accepted when, and only when, it is an act only the account holder can perform on the spot in real practice:
 (a) a by:user lifecycle transition of the base charter (e.g. the customer's own cancellation) together with the same-category consequence its base triggers/policies book (e.g. the window refund), with the deviation declared; or
 (b) a payment the holder completes personally through Harborline's secure checkout / payment link — PCI DSS practice: support staff never take card numbers by phone or chat, so a charge to a card or PayPal not stored on file, or any payment the holder must authorise, is completed by the holder — and the extended policy's own rule states that this payment is the holder's own act at checkout after the agent quotes it (declared as a scoped overwrite wherever a base PRODUCT-CHARTER rule sentence assigns that billing to the agent); or
 (c) the holder's own deposit of their own funds into account credit.
Not accepted: a customer "placing" an order or billing a line that the agent could charge to the stored method without the holder's action, i.e. an owner=user label with no in-person necessity; the persona must make the in-person necessity visible (e.g. the stored card expired/declined, or the holder wants to pay by a method not on file).
